The '''Derby of the Eternal Rivals''' ({{langx|el|Ντέρμπι των αιωνίων αντιπάλων}}), also called '''Mother of All Battles''' (Greek: Μητέρα των μαχών), is the name of the [[basketball]] [[local derby]] in [[Attica]] ([[Piraeus]] and [[Athens]]) between [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] and [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]]. The Greek powerhouses have won a combined [[EuroLeague#Titles by club|eleven EuroLeague titles]] since 1996, thus being among the [[FIBA European Champions Cup and EuroLeague records and statistics|most successful clubs in European basketball history]]. [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] basketball club has won seven [[EuroLeague#Titles by club|EuroLeague titles]] and [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] has won four [[EuroLeague#Titles by club|EuroLeague titles]]. Their rivalry inside and outside the Greek borders is considered one of the most thrilling in the basketball world.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=185&seasoncode=e2008#!preview Euroleague.net, Olympiacos-Panathinaikos 2009 Euroleague semifinal preview]</ref><ref>[http://ballineurope.com/the-great-rivalries-in-european-basketball-panathinaikos-vs-olympiakos/ Ballineurope.com, Great rivalries in European basketball: Panathinaikos vs. Olympiakos]</ref><ref>[http://ballineurope.com/great-rivalries-in-european-basketball-panathinaikos-vs-olympiakos-part-2/ Ballineurope.com, Great rivalries in European basketball: Panathinaikos vs. Olympiakos (Part 2)]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Gonzalez|first=John|date=2019-02-27|title=The Exile of Rick Pitino|url=https://www.theringer.com/2019/2/27/18242154/rick-pitino-panathinaikos-louisville-interview|access-date=2020-07-16|website=The Ringer|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/basketball/basket-league/2269691/olympiakos-panathinaikos-ntermpi-yp-arithmon-209-prasino | title=Ολυμπιακός - Παναθηναϊκός: Ντέρμπι υπ' αριθμόν 209, «πράσινο» το προβάδισμα &#124; Gazzetta }}</ref>

==History==

===Culture rivalry===
{{See also|Derby of the eternal enemies#History}}
The rivalry between the two top [[Greece|Greek]] clubs can be traced back to some social, cultural and regional differences. [[Panathinaikos A.O.|Panathinaikos]] comes from [[Athens]] and was considered the classic representative of the old Athenian society and culture. On the other hand, [[Olympiacos CFP|Olympiacos]] comes from [[Piraeus]] and used to represent the [[working class]]. However, this kind of clash was much more pronounced in the past, as the class differences between the fanbases have faded out and the social gap that once separated the two sides has closed over the years. Nowadays, both clubs boast fanbases that represent all the social classes.

===Basketball rivalry===
Panathinaikos and Olympiacos are two successful basketball teams in Greece. These two teams are long standing rivals and are successful clubs in Greek basketball. They have competed against each other at professional level for more years than any other teams in the country itself.

Their rivalry is highly credited, especially in the 1990s-2000s, when they met each other in several [[Season (sports)#Regular season|regular season]] and [[playoff]] series, and in some [[EuroLeague]] matches which marked their history.
